clue.text: What to do during street to-dos?

parts.note: during means in, as in 'in the night'
to-dos are commotions or rows, which ructions also are

explanation.surface: A question about what happens during noisy rows out on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to-dos' looks like a list of tasks, which chimes with the definition, but here it means fusses or rows: RUCTIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Directions or orders tell a person what they should do, so the phrase is a fair paraphrase.

clue.text: Damages panels one's left propping up home

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece propping up another sits below it, so the home piece comes first

parts.note: at home means in, so home gives IN

indicators.note: left here means departed, so the letter for one is taken out of the panels

parts.note: juries are panels of people sitting in judgement
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A household where damaged panelling is holding the place up after someone moves out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one has', with 'left' meaning departed, not the opposite of right.
explanation.definitionFit: To injure is to harm or hurt, a synonym of damage used as a verb.

clue.text: Very little time for Oliver's desire?

definitions.meaning: a moment or a tick, sixtieths of a minute
Oliver Twist famously asked for more food: a second helping

explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Twist, the Dickens orphan, holds out his bowl and asks for more.
explanation.definitionFit: Seconds are both tiny units of time and further helpings of food, which Oliver craved.

clue.text: Stayed in bed to preserve muscle that's admired

indicators.note: to preserve something is to keep it safe within, so the bed-rest word holds the muscle

parts.note: someone who stayed in bed rested
pec is short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: Someone who stayed in bed to save their strength is admired for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Respected and admired are close synonyms, both meaning held in high regard.

clue.text: Company appearing doubly in need of a drink

indicators.note: appearing doubly means the company abbreviation is written out twice

explanation.surface: Guests appearing two at a time, all wanting a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot chocolate made from powdered cacao beans is a familiar bedtime drink.

clue.text: Complaint from good person going in peace

indicators.note: going means leaving, so the good person is taken out of the word for peace

parts.note: peace and quiet is stillness
ST, short for saint, is the crossword good person

explanation.surface: A grumble from a decent person who wants to depart in peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' looks like a grievance but means an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is a disorder or ailment, as in a chest complaint.

clue.text: Extra piercing seen as more curious when worn by this person

indicators.note: something worn by a person is on or around them, so the more curious word goes round the letter for this person

parts.note: nosier means more inquisitive
this person is the speaker, I

explanation.surface: An extra body piercing draws more curious looks when someone wears it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piercing' suggests jewellery, but here it is a shrill sound, and 'Extra' makes it comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: A piercing sound is loud and shrill, so one that is more so is louder.

clue.text: Fading rum dip gains when fruit is added

indicators.note: the fruit is added by being placed within the shuffled letters
rum means odd or strange, so these letters are put in a strange order

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A rum dip that improves once fruit goes into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the spirit, but it is the anagram signal: DIP GAINS becomes DISAPING, and PEAR goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fading is vanishing gradually from sight, slowly going away.

clue.text: Takes drugs popular with high-fliers around clubs

parts.note: something popular is in

indicators.note: around means the aircraft word is placed round the clubs letter

parts.note: jets are aircraft that fly high
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Wealthy jet-setters taking drugs in nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests nightclubs, but it is the card suit, C.
explanation.definitionFit: Injecting a drug is a way of taking it, by syringe into the body.

clue.text: Career giving one a buzz?

definitions.meaning: a career or vocation, someone's chosen work
giving someone a buzz is phoning them

explanation.walkthrough: 'buzz' looks like excitement, but it is a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocation is a profession; ringing someone up is telephoning them.

clue.text: Pompous secretary cuts unpaid childminders?

parts.note: grand can mean imposing or self-important
PA, personal assistant, is a secretary
rents are tears or cuts, as in rents in a garment

explanation.surface: A pompous secretary trims the pay of the nursery staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' reads as a verb but is the noun RENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandmas and grandpas often look after the grandchildren for free, a cheeky view of their role.

clue.text: Date entraps Republican with organised plan

indicators.note: something that entraps holds its catch inside, so the date word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a date or period of history is an age
ran, as in ran a business, means organised

explanation.surface: A date set up to snare a Republican, with a plan carefully organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' looks like an anagram signal, but it is RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things is to plan or organise them in advance.

clue.text: Place that has crime breaking out in two areas

indicators.note: in places the shuffled crime letters inside the two area letters

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, taken twice

indicators.note: breaking out suggests the letters escape their order and rearrange

explanation.surface: A place where crime is breaking out in two districts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' is about as vague a definition as there is; the wordplay does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A country is a place, and the definition is deliberately vague.

clue.text: Stick with small social media entries

parts.note: a stick or pole is a post

explanation.surface: Sticking with short updates on social media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a verb but is a wooden post.
explanation.definitionFit: Messages put up on a social network are called posts.

clue.text: Beloved certain to be in step

indicators.note: to be in means the certain word is put inside the step word

parts.note: a tread is a step, on a staircase or in walking
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A beloved partner sure to be in step on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured is held dear and cherished, as a beloved thing is.

clue.text: Wheel's to be mended before getting away from this place

indicators.note: something to be mended needs putting back together, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: The wheel needs fixing before the vehicle can get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be mended' rearranges WHEELS into ELSEWH.
explanation.definitionFit: Being somewhere other than here means being away from the present spot.

clue.text: Ace duettist reviewed in 'Points of View'

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the letters are looked at again and reordered

explanation.surface: A top-class duet singer is critiqued on the TV show Points of View.
explanation.walkthrough: Points of View is a long-running BBC programme of viewers' letters; 'reviewed' rearranges DUETTIST into TTITUDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinions or outlooks are viewpoints, so the plural noun fits the definition.

clue.text: Little European wriggling baby

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A small European baby squirming about.
explanation.definitionFit: A young frog wriggles in the pond before growing legs: an infant amphibian.

clue.text: Tchaikovsky's silent introduction leads to his money problem

indicators.note: the introduction to the name is its first letter, which, in the composer's name, is not sounded

parts.note: the introduction leads on to his money; the composer was Russian, and Russia's currency is the rouble

explanation.surface: The composer's quiet opening leads to financial difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble is a difficulty or bother, so it means a problem.

clue.text: Conservative, old, male, married? Answer is something in between

explanation.surface: A conservative old married man is asked about something in between.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark sits between parts of a sentence, separating clauses or items.

clue.text: Famously moreish grub? Feasted on and off, after having part by mouth

indicators.note: after having means the first piece is placed before the next

parts.note: the chin is the part of the face just below the mouth

indicators.note: on and off means taking alternate letters only

explanation.surface: Diners feasting on and off on tasty grub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on and off' takes ESE from Feasted. The definition plays on the joke that a takeaway from this cuisine leaves one hungry soon after.
explanation.definitionFit: Food from China, or Chinese takeaway, is said to leave you wanting more an hour later.

clue.text: Insect queen's spoils

parts.note: a moth is an insect
ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina, with the 's of the possessive

explanation.surface: An insect queen's spoils of war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' looks like a noun (loot), but it is a verb meaning pampers.
explanation.definitionFit: To mother someone is to pamper and fuss over them, to spoil them.

clue.text: Sculpted Rodins, including 'Duck Under a Roof'

indicators.note: including means the shuffled letters go round the duck letter
sculpted means shaped anew, so these letters are reformed

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: Rodin's sculptures include one titled Duck Under a Roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sculpted' rearranges RODINS into INDORS, and O goes inside. A duck is a batter's score of nought in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sheltered under a roof means being inside a building.

clue.text: Petals lacking a liquid dropped off

indicators.note: liquid suggests the letters flow freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Petals with no liquid to feed them have dropped from the flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking a' removes A from PETALS, and 'liquid' rearranges PETLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping off is falling asleep, so the past tense fits slept.

clue.text: Game involving cards shown by the French referee's stand-by?

parts.note: whist is a card game
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A card game with a French referee standing by.
explanation.definitionFit: A football referee relies on the device blown to stop play, a trusty standby.

clue.text: Discussed bargain that's delivered as one leaves

indicators.note: discussed means spoken about, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a bargain is a good buy

explanation.surface: Talking over a bargain that gets delivered as you go.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell is said at parting, spoken as someone departs.

clue.text: Brazilian player not using head and hands — feet finally bringing gold perhaps

indicators.note: not using head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Pele was Brazil's famous footballer
hands are workers, men

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter

explanation.surface: A Brazilian footballer who does not use head or hands, only his feet, wins gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Pele lacking his head gives ELE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold is an example of a chemical substance in the periodic table.

clue.text: Article put by not at all diminished yet

indicators.note: put by means the article is placed beside, after, the not at all piece

parts.note: never means not at all
the is the definite article
less means reduced or diminished

explanation.surface: An article put aside, not at all reduced yet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean however or all the same, contrastive adverbs.
